item.title: Daily Gaming & Tech Brief — September 17, 2026
item.description:
1. GAME & TECH NEWS

GAME NEWS

September's release calendar is entering its busiest stretch, with a dense sequence of PC releases, Early Access launches and major updates. Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, The Guild 1 Remake: Europa 1410 and other releases are arriving during a crowded September schedule.

Steam's Party-Based RPG Fest is also running through September 21, putting party-focused RPGs, demos and discounts in the spotlight.

TECH NEWS

Huawei says demand for its Ascend AI hardware is exceeding production capacity in China, while Apple is reportedly exploring enterprise AI servers based on custom silicon.

GNOME 51 has launched with graphics, frame-scheduling and capture improvements, while Linux gaming infrastructure continues expanding beyond traditional x86 PCs.

2. STEAM SALE / EVENT

Steam Party-Based RPG Fest — September 14–21

Steam's Party-Based RPG Fest focuses on party-based RPGs and includes discounts, demos and featured games.

3. XODUS

Xodus remains an active open-source project focused on bringing Xbox PC and Game Pass software to Linux and macOS. Login, package downloading and license acquisition are documented working components, while Xbox runtime compatibility, MSIXVC packaging and game execution remain active development areas.

Progress: active development toward game execution

4. FREE GAMES

Astral Ascent and Luftrausers were the Epic Games Store free-to-keep games for September 10–17. Amazon Prime's September 17 drop includes DOOM Eternal, Rims Racing and Wall World 2.

5. LINUX APPS

GNOME 51, Sunshine and Nuclear are notable Linux software picks for the day.

6. PIRACY SCENE

Denuvo's lawsuit against the anonymous figure known as voices38 alleges circumvention of Denuvo Anti-Tamper in at least 26 PC games. The case is at an early stage and the allegations have not been established as facts by a court.

Separately, publishers continue removing Denuvo from older games, making DRM lifecycle policy an ongoing part of the PC gaming scene. Community claims about releases or bypasses are treated separately from confirmed legal filings and publisher updates.

item.title: Daily Gaming & Tech Brief — September 18, 2026
item.description:
1. GAME & TECH NEWS

GAME NEWS

GTA 6 is looming over a crowded October release period, while Active Matter has launched on PC, PS5 and Xbox. Patlabor: The Case Files launched on PC and PS5, and September 18 brings releases including NASCAR 26, The Walking Dead: Streets of Survival and Moomintroll: Winter's Warmth.

Fortnite's Kingdom Hearts crossover is live, bringing Sora, Riku, Kairi and Roxas content plus a Kingdom Key Mythic. Dune: Awakening is scheduled to receive its single-player mode on September 22.

Xodus continues work toward Xbox PC/Game Pass game execution on Linux, with login, package downloading and license acquisition working while runtime and Wine integration remain major engineering areas.

TECH NEWS

Apple is reportedly considering an enterprise AI inference server using planned M8 Ultra chips and potentially Nvidia NVLink Fusion, with a reported long-term target. Huawei says China's AI-compute supply still cannot meet domestic demand.

GNOME 51 is released, Nvidia GeForce support is appearing in SteamOS development, and Valve is expanding SteamOS beyond Proton with FEX and Android compatibility work for Steam Frame.

2. STEAM SALE / EVENT

Steam Party-Based RPG Fest — September 14–21

The current official Steam event runs through September 21 and includes party-based RPG discounts, demos and featured games. Notable discounts include Baldur's Gate 3, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and older Expeditions titles. Tokyo Game Show is not being counted as a Steam event.

3. XODUS

Xodus documents working login, package downloading and license acquisition. Its open-source Xbox runtime, patched Wine/Proton work, MSIXVC2 support and executable decryption remain important development areas.

Progress: active development toward game execution

4. FREE GAMES

Shogun Showdown and Mindcop are free to keep on Epic from September 17–24, 2026.

  • DOOM Eternal — Microsoft Store code — September 17
  • Rims Racing — Epic Games Store — September 17
  • Wall World 2 — Amazon Games App — September 17
  • Hue — Epic Games Store — September 24
  • The Da Vinci Cryptex — Legacy Games Code — September 24
  • High on Life — Epic Games Store — September 24

No additional confirmed Steam 100%-free-to-keep giveaway or notable temporary GOG giveaway was verified.

5. LINUX APPS

GNOME 51 brings graphics and capture improvements. Beam Eye Tracker adds Linux/macOS eye and head tracking using ordinary cameras. lsfg-vk provides Linux frame-generation functionality for Vulkan applications.

6. PIRACY SCENE

Denuvo lawsuit against voices38

Denuvo filed suit on September 14, 2026, against the anonymous figure known as voices38, alleging circumvention of Denuvo Anti-Tamper in at least 26 PC games. The complaint invokes DMCA anti-circumvention provisions, and the defendant's identity has not been publicly established.

Broader DRM developments

The lawsuit is only one part of the current scene. Publishers continue removing Denuvo from older games, new releases continue using DRM, and Linux/SteamOS compatibility remains a separate pressure point.

Unverified claims

Community claims about rapid Denuvo bypasses, release groups or specific mechanisms are not consistently independently verified and are kept separate from confirmed developments.
